name: Colorado Microcircuits
old_description: By automating every step of the IC assembly process we work to increase reliability and drive costs down.
about:
Colorado Microcircuits operates a custom-built facility in Loveland, Colorado. The company, known as CMI, specializes in highly automated contract assembly of microwave and RF semiconductors. No founding year or founders are disclosed in public materials.

CMI provides assembly of single and multi-die components using off-the-shelf or custom packages, including ceramic, air cavity lead frames, overmold lead frames, and high-performance laminates. Its processes cover die attach, wire bonding, mixed assembly of integrated circuits and surface-mount components, high thermal conductivity epoxies, short/tuned/stacked wires, stacked die, and GGI flip chip. The company reports manufacturing volumes ranging from thousands to millions of units, leveraging industry-standard automated semiconductor assembly equipment in an ISO 9001 compliant environment.

The company serves the RF and microwave semiconductor market, describing itself as a key assembly partner for industry leaders in that sector. It targets customers needing an onshore U.S. partner for commercial volumes and competitive pricing, emphasizing proximity to any U.S. customer.

CMI states its niche is innovative air cavity packaging, and that automating every step of the IC assembly process increases reliability and drives down costs. It aims to provide turnkey solutions with short production lead times, and positions its high-volume onshore capability as a way to mitigate geopolitical supply chain risks.
